items.title: William "Ba Ba" Ridgley Interview, 1959-06-02
items.q: And then he gave up the coinette playing and old man Welch came back again... And he played along in Silver Leaf Band with me.

ctx.x: Do you remember about, excuse me, what year that was about? Was that...

That could have been about 1910. 1910, when you joined the Silver Leaf. Silver Leaf Band. I was still living in Jefferson Paris. And then I moved to New Orleans in 1911. And I was still with Silver Leaf Band. And Mr. Welch, he was a sickly man and he gave up the coinette playing. And we got over to the fellow by the name of Hippolyte Charles. He played coinette for us a while. And then he gave up the coinette playing and old man Welch came back again. And old man Welch made me to know Celestine. He said he was a…
You had already called it the Tuxedo Band though before you started the tuxedos. Is that right? Yes. And he was a big help to us.

items.title: William "Ba Ba" Ridgley Interview, 1959-06-02
items.q: Professor Welch then, he brought us to New Orleans and joined us in with the Silver Leaf Band... And Mr. Welch, he was a sickly man and he gave up the coinette playing... old man Welch came back again.

ctx.x: Just about where was that in the Jefferson?

About one mile and a quarter out of the city limit. And we used to have to meet Professor Umphrey every Sunday morning about 9 o'clock. We had a little road cart. We'd carry him, flurry and two. And so the people that I wait for, they give us a place that we could have our practice, take our lessons, and might near every night while we was there playing and doing the best that we could. And so Professor Umphrey, I had to take him back in for it. And he advised me to buy a trombone. And I agreed to do so. And he…
